findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

Recovery treats any delivered output for the run as proof that every consumed item was answered. If the owner sends an early reply, then consumes a follow-up and crashes before the runner receives that continuation, this branch keeps the follow-up consumed and marks its pending continuation command applied. The next turn cannot take it. Track which items reached the runner or release unanswered follow-ups independently of earlier output.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The spawned processes only call takeInput and getMessagesByIds, then exit. The active-turn follow-up test creates both admission workers in one process and mocks the runner's continuation input. Neither test exercises two independent runtime workers delivering a follow-up to a runner and reply, so the required two-process no-loss/no-duplication behavior remains unproven.
findings.title: Not done: two-process end-to-end no-loss/no-duplication test

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

The active-turn path consumes every non-control item and builds a text-only continuation. A message carrying responseSchema or agentControls therefore loses those settings before reaching the runner, while its admission item stays consumed. Keep such requests for a new turn that can pass their settings to runAgent.
findings.title: Preserve schema and agent controls on active-turn requests

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

takeInput selects items by receiveOrder, but this new sort gives provider timestamps precedence. A delayed attachment or a provider timestamp that moves backward can therefore appear before messages received earlier in the same batch. Sort by receiveOrder when available so the agent sees the recorded arrival order.
findings.title: Present taken messages in receive order

findings.body:
chunk 1/3:

This new file stores a prior review result and task status. It is outside the permitted paths and is not needed for the runtime switch, migration, tests, or decisions. Remove it from the change.
findings.title: Remove the review-state file outside the allowed scope

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

Channel intake saves work items under the runtime app ID (`channel-persistence-handlers.ts:224-226`), but this new take scopes them with `turnAppId`, which `command-override-route-key.ts:37` derives from the chat JID and defaults to `default`. A normal Telegram or Slack JID in a non-default app therefore never matches its saved items. The turn sees an empty batch and replies to nothing; recovery repeats the same mismatch. Use the admission item's actual app scope.
findings.title: Not done: No message is lost or given twice.

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

If a turn delivered some output, then a follow-up was taken and routed before the worker died, `hasDeliveredOutputForRun` is true. Recovery leaves that follow-up consumed and marks pending continuation commands applied, even though the runner may never have given the follow-up to the model. The next turn cannot take it. Delivery of an earlier reply is insufficient evidence that later input was handled; recovery needs per-follow-up confirmation or must release unconfirmed items.
findings.title: Release unconfirmed follow-ups when recovering a turn that already replied

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The new failure handler returns without releasing consumed input whenever `acknowledgeFailedTurn` is true, even if `outputSentToUser` is false. `group-processing.ts:764-767` sets that flag on an ordinary exhausted final retry. Thus a turn that fails silently before replying leaves its messages permanently consumed, contrary to the required next-turn retry behavior.
findings.title: Release input after a final retry that sent no reply

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

The added child processes call `takeInput` and `getMessagesByIds` directly, then exit. They never run admission, route a continuation, execute a turn, or deliver a reply. The separate two-worker follow-up case creates both workers in one process with a stubbed `runAgent`. Consequently these tests cannot catch message loss or duplicate delivery during a real two-process owner handoff, which this part explicitly requires the e2e test to prove.
findings.title: Not done: two-process no-loss end-to-end test

findings.body:
chunk 3/3:

`takeInput` selects items by `receiveOrder`, but this sort moves a later-received item ahead whenever its provider timestamp is in an earlier second. The new unit test even expects that inversion. Delayed media or provider timestamps can therefore present a burst to the agent out of received order. Sort by `receiveOrder` for recorded items.
findings.title: Preserve database receive order in the turn prompt
